newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-off $0.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower amid continued pressure from weak pork demand and unprofitable packer operating margins, livestock dealers said.
"It doesn't look good for the first part of next week, that's for sure," one Illinois hog buyer said.
Larger-than-expected marketings Thursday further weighed on cash hog prices Friday and provided packers with enough hogs to meet Friday and Saturday slaughter needs, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at the plant could range $57.00 to $57.50, they said.
Illinois hogs at the plant were seen with a top of $56.00 to $56.50 and Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants were seen at $57.00 to $57.50, dealers said.
Increased pork production this week weighed on pork prices as did competition from beef for the retail dollar, they said.

Pork production this week at 310.8 million lbs was 1.2 percent above last week's level of 307.0 million, USDA reported. Boneless pork loins with a 1/4-inch trim weighing 18-22 lbs at midday Friday were quoted at 134.00 per cwt, down $2.00 for the week, USDA statistics showed.
